headline_hook: Washington Pulls the Plug on Fable as Kimi and Fusion Race to Fill the Void
preview_topics: why open weights are suddenly insurance

pick_of_the_day.thesis: The Fable ban isn't a national security story — it's a cloud wars story. Amazon's CEO lobbied officials to restrict his own portfolio company's flagship product, revealing that in the age of AI, your largest investor can also become your most effective regulator.

model_literacy.relevance: The Fable ban was possible because API access can be revoked with a single directive. Open-weight models like Llama or Mistral can't be 'turned off' once downloaded. This distinction — who holds the kill switch — is now the central question in AI infrastructure decisions.

items.title: US Government Orders Fable 5 and Mythos 5 Suspended for All Foreign Nationals
items.angle: The most aggressive AI export control action ever — not a future regulation but an immediate kill switch on live API access affecting every non-US Anthropic customer overnight
items.key_fact: Suspension covers all foreign nationals, whether inside or outside the US, under national security authorities

items.title: Amazon CEO's Lobbying Directly Triggered the Fable Crackdown
items.angle: WSJ investigation reveals the corporate politics behind the directive — Amazon lobbied to restrict its own investment's most powerful product, rewriting the rules on investor-lab dynamics
items.key_fact: Amazon CEO's direct conversations with US officials precipitated the export control action

items.title: Anthropic's Official Statement on the Fable and Mythos Suspension
items.angle: Anthropic's compliance response provides the full scope — what's suspended, who's affected, and what comes next
items.key_fact: Official statement confirms full compliance with the directive and outlines the access suspension timeline

items.title: Latent Space: Fable and Mythos 'Officially Too Dangerous to Release'
items.angle: The industry commentary layer — what happens when a government declares your best model a national security risk
items.key_fact: First major AI newsletter to frame the suspension as a precedent for all frontier labs, not just Anthropic

items.title: Mollick: Don't Expect This Ban to Help Open-Source AI
items.angle: The contrarian take — if Mythos-level models are deemed risky, no government including China's will want them open-weight either
items.key_fact: If the risk framing sticks, open-source faces the same regulatory pressure as closed-source

items.title: Google DeepMind Launches European Robotics Accelerator with Gemini Access
items.angle: Physical AI enters the accelerator phase — 15 startups get Gemini Robotics models, signaling Google's embodied intelligence bet
items.key_fact: 15 startups in a three-month program with access to Google's full AI stack and Gemini Robotics models

items.title: Kimi 2.7 Code Drops 'Mind-Blowing' Agentic Coding Benchmarks
items.angle: Arriving at the exact moment Fable access gets restricted — if benchmarks hold, Kimi 2.7 becomes the default alternative for teams losing their best coding model
items.key_fact: Benchmark results reportedly rival or exceed Fable 5 on agentic coding tasks

items.title: Fusion API Claims Fable-Level Deep Research at Half the Cost
items.angle: Launched the same day as the Fable ban — if performance claims hold, Fusion becomes the first credible drop-in for deep research workflows
items.key_fact: Claims Fable-level performance on deep research tasks at 50% of the cost

items.title: OpenAI Adds an AI Docs Agent to Its Developer Platform

items.title: Frontier Models Fail a Simple Instruction-Following Test
items.angle: GPT-5.5 and Fable both refuse to change 'three words' to 'four' — revealing systematic over-alignment that persists at the frontier
items.key_fact: Both GPT-5.5 Pro Extended and Fable Max fail the same instruction-following edge case
